title.zh: 卷398 列傳一百八十五 宗室祥厚 霍隆武 福珠洪阿 恩长 陈胜元 祁宿藻 陈克让 刘同缨 瑞昌 杰纯 锡龄阿
title.en: Volume 398 Biographies 185: Zong Shixianghou, Huo Longwu, Fu Zhu Hong A, En Zhang, Chen Shengyuan, Qi Suzao, Chen Kerang, Liu Tongying, Rui Chang, Jie Chun, Xi Ling A
title.raw: 卷398 列傳一百八十五 宗室祥厚 霍隆武 福珠洪阿 恩长 陈胜元 祁宿藻 陈克让 刘同缨 瑞昌 杰纯 锡龄阿

sentences.zh: 列傳一百八十五

translations.literal: Biography 185
translations.idiomatic: Biography 185

sentences.zh: 宗室祥厚霍隆武福珠洪阿恩長陳勝元祁宿藻陳克讓劉同纓

translations.literal: Imperial clansman Xianghou, Huo Longwu, Fu Zhu Hong'a, En Chang, Chen Shengyuan, Qi Suzao, Chen Kerang, and Liu Tongying
translations.idiomatic: Imperial clansman Xianghou; Huo Longwu; Fu Zhu Hong'a; En Chang; Chen Shengyuan; Qi Suzao; Chen Kerang; and Liu Tongying

sentences.zh: 瑞昌杰純錫齡阿

translations.literal: Rui Chang, Jie Chun, and Xi Ling'a
translations.idiomatic: Rui Chang, Jie Chun, and Xi Ling'a

sentences.zh: 宗室祥厚，隸鑲紅旗，襲騎都尉世職，授鑾儀衛整儀尉。

translations.literal: The imperial clansman Xianghou belonged to the Bordered Red Banner, inherited the hereditary office of Cavalry Commandant of the Fourth Rank, and was appointed a Ceremonial Guard orderly officer of the Imperial Procession Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Xianghou, an imperial clansman of the Bordered Red Banner, inherited a hereditary cavalry commandant's rank and was appointed an orderly officer in the Imperial Procession Guard.

sentences.zh: 累擢鑲紅旗蒙古副都統，歷山海關、熊岳、金州副都統。

translations.literal: He was promoted repeatedly to Mongol deputy lieutenant-general of the Bordered Red Banner and served in succession as deputy lieutenant-general at Shanhaiguan, Xiongyue, and Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Through successive promotions he became Mongol deputy lieutenant-general of the Bordered Red Banner, holding deputy lieutenant-general posts at Shanhaiguan, Xiongyue, and Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 道光二十八年，擢江寧將軍。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year of the Daoguang reign, he was promoted to military governor of Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: In 1848 he was appointed military governor of Jiangning (Nanjing).

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年正月，粵匪既陷武昌，兩江總督陸建瀛赴上游督師，祥厚偕江蘇巡撫楊文定留守江寧。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year of the Xianfeng reign, after the Cantonese rebels had already taken Wuchang, the governor-general of Liangjiang, Lu Jianying, went upstream to supervise the army, while Xianghou together with Jiangsu governor Yang Wending remained to hold Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of 1853, after the Taiping rebels captured Wuchang, Liangjiang governor-general Lu Jianying marched upstream to take command, leaving Xianghou and Jiangsu governor Yang Wending to defend Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 賊已蔽江而下，壽春鎮總兵恩長戰歿，建瀛遽退，文定亦不候旨迳赴鎮江。

translations.literal: The rebels had already covered the river and swept downstream; Shouchun garrison commander En Chang died in battle; Jianying retreated abruptly; and Wending likewise, without awaiting imperial instruction, went straight to Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were already bearing down the Yangtze; Shouchun commander En Chang was killed in action; Jianying fell back in haste; and Wending, without waiting for orders, went straight to Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 祥厚偕副都統霍隆武、提督福珠洪阿、布政使祁宿藻疏言：「督臣藉口江寧吃緊，趕回佈置，沿途險要，並不屯紮，上駛師船，一概撤回，專守水路之東西梁山。

translations.literal: Xianghou together with deputy lieutenant-general Huo Longwu, provincial military commissioner Fu Zhu Hong'a, and provincial administration commissioner Qi Suzao memorialized: 'The governor-general, citing the urgency of Jiangning, hurried back to make arrangements, yet along the critical points of the route he stationed no troops, recalled all upstream war junks, and concentrated solely on guarding the Eastern and Western Liang Hills on the water route.
translations.idiomatic: Xianghou, Huo Longwu, Fu Zhu Hong'a, and Qi Suzao jointly memorialized: 'The governor-general, pleading the crisis at Nanjing, rushed back to arrange defenses, yet posted no troops at any strategic point along the route, recalled every upstream war junk, and concentrated only on the Eastern and Western Liang Hills on the river.

sentences.zh: 蕪湖為江蘇門戶，亦不設防。

translations.literal: Wuhu, the gateway of Jiangsu, was likewise left undefended.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhu, Jiangsu's gateway, was left undefended as well.

sentences.zh: 十八日隻身抵省，遂致闔城驚擾。

translations.literal: On the eighteenth he arrived at the provincial capital alone, thereby throwing the whole city into alarm and turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighteenth he reached the capital alone, throwing the entire city into panic.

sentences.zh: 臣等函勸速統舟師迎擊，乃督臣晏坐衙齋，三日不覆。

translations.literal: We wrote urging him to gather the fleet at once and meet the attack, yet the governor-general sat idle in his yamen and for three days gave no reply.
translations.idiomatic: We urged him by letter to rally the fleet and strike at once, but the governor-general sat idle in his yamen and did not answer for three days.

sentences.zh: 撫臣執意移駐鎮江，挽留不顧，民情加倍驚惶。

translations.literal: The governor insisted on moving his headquarters to Zhenjiang and would not stay though we detained him; popular alarm doubled.
translations.idiomatic: The governor insisted on moving to Zhenjiang and ignored our pleas to remain; public alarm doubled.

sentences.zh: 自今固結民心，尚恐緩急難恃；

translations.literal: From this time on, even if the people's hearts are firmly bound, we still fear they cannot be relied on in an emergency;
translations.idiomatic: Even if hearts are rallied from this day forward, we still fear the populace cannot be counted on when crisis comes;

sentences.zh: 若任其紛紛遷徙，土匪因而竊發，奸細尤易勾結。

translations.literal: if they are allowed to scatter in flight, local bandits will seize the chance to rise, and spies will find it especially easy to make contact.
translations.idiomatic: if people are allowed to flee in disorder, local bandits will rise, and enemy agents will find it all the easier to conspire.

sentences.zh: 是未禦外侮，將成內變。

translations.literal: Thus before the foreign foe is repelled, an internal upheaval will take shape.
translations.idiomatic: We would fail to repel the invader only to face rebellion within.

sentences.zh: 現在督撫臣首鼠兩端，進退無據，以致省城震動。

translations.literal: At present the governor and governor-general are irresolute on both sides and advance or retreat without firm ground, so that the provincial capital is shaken.
translations.idiomatic: The governor and governor-general now waver between two courses and advance or retreat without resolve, shaking the whole capital.

sentences.zh: 雖有旗兵志切同仇，無如兵力太單。

translations.literal: Although the garrison bannermen are eager to share the common hatred, there is no help for it that their forces are too few.
translations.idiomatic: Though the garrison bannermen burn to fight, their numbers are far too few.

sentences.zh: 賊船順流下竄，朝發夕至，守禦萬分緊迫，督同道府等官及八旗協領，激勵官兵，安慰居民，竭盡血誠，認真辦理。

translations.literal: The rebel ships race downstream; they depart at dawn and arrive by evening; defense is desperately urgent. The governor, circuit intendants, prefects, and other officials together with the Eight Banners assistant commandants are rousing officers and soldiers, comforting the residents, exhausting their loyal effort, and handling matters conscientiously.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel vessels run downstream and may reach us overnight; defense is desperately tight. The governor, circuit and prefectural officials, and Eight Banners assistant commandants are encouraging the troops, reassuring the people, and doing all they can in earnest.

sentences.zh: 請飭琦善、陳金綬迅速繞出賊前，協力堵剿，以固省城根本，維持南北大局。

translations.literal: We beg that Qi Shan and Chen Jinshou be ordered to swing swiftly ahead of the rebels and join in blocking and suppressing them, to secure the root of the provincial capital and uphold the larger situation north and south.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that Qi Shan and Chen Jinshou be ordered to circle ahead of the rebels and help block them, to secure the capital and steady the empire north and south.

sentences.zh: 」疏入，詔逮建瀛治罪，命祥厚兼署總督，與霍隆武、福珠洪阿、祁宿藻悉心防禦，以在籍前廣西巡撫鄒鳴鶴熟悉賊情，命同籌辦。

translations.literal: ' When the memorial was received, an edict ordered Jianying arrested and punished, appointed Xianghou acting governor-general, and directed him together with Huo Longwu, Fu Zhu Hong'a, and Qi Suzao to devote themselves to defense; because the former Guangxi governor Zou Minghe, then at home, knew the rebels well, he was ordered to assist in planning.
translations.idiomatic: ' On receipt of the memorial, the throne ordered Jianying arrested, made Xianghou acting governor-general, and told him, Huo Longwu, Fu Zhu Hong'a, and Qi Suzao to organize the defense; Zou Minghe, a former Guangxi governor at home on leave who knew the rebels, was ordered to help plan.

sentences.zh: 江寧城周九十六里，合旗、漢兵僅五千，城外江寧鎮、龍江關、上河分駐鄉勇不及三千，臨時召募，皆不足恃。

translations.literal: The Jiangning wall measured ninety-six li in circuit; banner and Han troops together numbered only five thousand; outside the city the militia posted at Jiangning town, Longjiang Pass, and Shanghe totaled fewer than three thousand; men recruited on the spot were all unreliable.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing's walls ran ninety-six li; banner and Han troops together numbered only five thousand; militia at Jiangning town, Longjiang Pass, and Shanghe outside the walls were under three thousand; emergency recruits could not be trusted.

sentences.zh: 賊過蕪湖，福山鎮總兵陳勝元率舟師戰歿，遂無御者，長驅直抵城下，四面環攻。

translations.literal: After the rebels passed Wuhu, Fushan garrison commander Chen Shengyuan led the naval force and died in battle; thereafter there was no one to oppose them, and they drove straight to the foot of the walls and attacked on all sides.
translations.idiomatic: Past Wuhu, Fushan commander Chen Shengyuan led the fleet to battle and was killed; with no one left to stop them, the rebels swept to the walls and besieged the city on every side.

sentences.zh: 守逾旬，賊於儀鳳門穴地轟城，傾十餘丈，復由水西門、旱西門、南門緣梯而登，城遂陷。

translations.literal: The defense lasted more than ten days; the rebels undermined the wall at Yifeng Gate and blasted it down for more than a dozen zhang; they then scaled the wall by ladders at the Water West Gate, Dry West Gate, and South Gate, and the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: After more than ten days, the rebels tunneled under Yifeng Gate and blew down a dozen-odd zhang of wall, then climbed in by ladder at the Water West, Dry West, and South gates, and the city was lost.

sentences.zh: 祥厚偕霍隆武斂兵守駐防城，婦女皆助戰，逾日亦陷。

translations.literal: Xianghou together with Huo Longwu gathered troops to hold the garrison quarter; women also helped fight; after a day that too fell.
translations.idiomatic: Xianghou and Huo Longwu drew off troops to hold the Manchu garrison city; women fought beside them; a day later that too fell.

sentences.zh: 祥厚手刃數賊，身被數十創，死之。

translations.literal: Xianghou himself cut down several rebels, received several dozen wounds, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Xianghou killed several rebels with his own hand, took dozens of wounds, and died.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈太子太保，予二等輕車都尉世職，諡忠勇。

translations.literal: When the affair was reported, he was posthumously granted Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and a hereditary second-rank commandant of light chariots, with the posthumous title Zhongyong (Loyal and Brave).
translations.idiomatic: On report of his death he was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, granted a hereditary second-rank light-chariot commandancy, and given the posthumous name Zhongyong (Loyal and Brave).

sentences.zh: 入祀京師昭忠祠，於江寧建專祠，死事者附祀焉。

translations.literal: He was entered in the capital Shrine of Loyalty and Martyrdom; a special shrine was built for him at Jiangning, and those who died in the affair were attached for joint worship.
translations.idiomatic: He was enshrined in the capital Shrine of Loyalty and Martyrdom, given a private shrine at Nanjing, with other victims worshipped there beside him.

sentences.zh: 霍隆武，鈕祜祿氏，滿洲鑲黃旗人，福州駐防。

translations.literal: Huo Longwu, of the Niohuru clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner, garrisoned at Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huo Longwu of the Niohuru clan was a Bordered Yellow Banner Manchu from the Fuzhou garrison.

sentences.zh: 由武舉前鋒校歷官福建水師旗營協領。

translations.literal: From military graduate and vanguard company officer he rose through offices to assistant commandant of the Fujian naval forces banner camp.
translations.idiomatic: Starting as a military graduate and vanguard company officer, he rose to assistant commandant of the Fujian naval banner camp.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，擢江寧副都統。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng he was promoted to deputy lieutenant-general of Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: In 1851 he was made deputy lieutenant-general of Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 賊圍城，偕祥厚登陴固守，歷十餘晝夜，外城陷，同守內城，策馬督戰，受傷墮，力竭陣亡，贈都統，予騎都尉兼雲騎尉世職，諡果毅。

translations.literal: When the rebels besieged the city, he joined Xianghou on the battlements in a stubborn defense lasting more than ten days and nights; when the outer city fell they defended the inner city together; he spurred his horse to direct the fight, was wounded and fell, and died in battle when his strength was spent; he was posthumously granted lieutenant-general, given a hereditary commandant of cavalry combined with commandant of the cloud cavalry, and honored with the posthumous title Guoyi (Resolute).
translations.idiomatic: When the city was besieged he and Xianghou held the walls for ten days and nights; after the outer city fell they held the inner city; he led from horseback, was wounded and fell, and died when his strength gave out; posthumously made lieutenant-general with a combined cavalry and cloud-cavalry commandancy, posthumous name Guoyi (Resolute).

sentences.zh: 當時駐防旗兵戰最力。

translations.literal: At that time the garrison banner troops fought with the greatest effort.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison bannermen fought harder than anyone.

sentences.zh: 錫齡額者，事母孝，將軍本智異之，擢為參領。

translations.literal: Xi Ling'e was filial toward his mother; Military Governor Benzhi took note of him and promoted him to company commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Ling'e was devoted to his mother; Military Governor Benzhi noticed him and made him a company commandant.

sentences.zh: 曰：「求忠臣必於孝子之門。

translations.literal: He said: 'Seek loyal ministers at the door of filial sons.
translations.idiomatic: He said, 'Loyal ministers are to be sought in the houses of filial sons.

sentences.zh: 」事急，戒其妻：「國家豢養，無所報；

translations.literal: ' When the crisis came he warned his wife: 'The state has maintained us, and we have nothing with which to repay it;
translations.idiomatic: ' When crisis came he told his wife, 'The state has fed us and we have not repaid it;

sentences.zh: 脫不利，當闔門死。

translations.literal: if things go badly, the whole household must die together.
translations.idiomatic: if things go ill, the whole household must die together.

sentences.zh: 」自守城，即不返家，舉室皆殉。

translations.literal: ' From the time he took up the defense of the city he did not return home, and the entire family perished with him.
translations.idiomatic: ' Once he took the wall he never went home again, and his whole family died with him.

sentences.zh: 炳元，官佐領，勇力冠軍。

translations.literal: Bingyuan, an assistant commandant, was foremost in the army in courage and strength.
translations.idiomatic: Bingyuan, an assistant commandant, was the strongest fighter in the garrison.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳門之陷，率死士奮鬥，賊為之卻，忽有狙擊者，殞於陣。

translations.literal: When Yifeng Gate fell he led dare-to-die troops in a fierce fight and drove the rebels back; suddenly a sniper struck, and he fell on the field.
translations.idiomatic: At the fall of Yifeng Gate he led picked men in a fierce charge and forced the rebels back until a sniper killed him in the melee.

sentences.zh: 賊破內城，屠戮尤慘，男婦幾無孑遺。

translations.literal: When the rebels broke the inner city the slaughter was especially savage; scarcely a man or woman was left alive.
translations.idiomatic: When the inner city fell the slaughter was especially terrible; almost no man or woman survived.

sentences.zh: 福珠洪阿，蘇完瓜爾佳氏，滿洲正黃旗人，副都統佛安子。

translations.literal: Fu Zhu Hong'a, of the Suwan Guwalgiya clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner and son of deputy lieutenant-general Fo'an.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zhu Hong'a of the Suwan Guwalgiya clan was a Plain Yellow Banner Manchu and son of Deputy Lieutenant-General Fo'an.

sentences.zh: 由鑾儀衛整儀尉累擢總兵，歷鎮筸、伊犁、西寧、天津諸鎮。

translations.literal: From Ceremonial Guard orderly officer he was promoted repeatedly to regional commander and served in succession at Zhenqian, Ili, Xining, Tianjin, and other garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: From an Imperial Procession Guard orderly he rose to regional commander, commanding in turn at Zhenqian, Ili, Xining, Tianjin, and other posts.

sentences.zh: 道光末，授江南提督，調陝西。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daoguang reign he was appointed provincial military commissioner of Jiangnan and transferred to Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Daoguang he became Jiangnan provincial military commissioner, then was transferred to Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 粵匪起，江南籌防，仍調回舊任，駐守省城，所部兵僅數百人。

translations.literal: When the Cantonese rebels rose, Jiangnan made preparations for defense and he was transferred back to his former post, garrisoning the provincial capital; the troops under his command numbered only a few hundred.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebellion broke out, Jiangnan recalled him to his old post at the capital with only a few hundred men under him.

sentences.zh: 地雷發，迎擊於城缺，斬悍賊，而諸門先後破。

translations.literal: When the land mine exploded he met the attack at the breach in the wall and cut down fierce rebels, but the gates in succession were broken through.
translations.idiomatic: When the mine went off he met the enemy at the breach and killed fierce rebels, but the gates fell one after another.

sentences.zh: 賊四面至，往來巷戰，死之。

translations.literal: The rebels came from all four sides; he fought back and forth in the lanes and died.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels poured in from every side; he fought street by street and died.

sentences.zh: 贈太子少保，予二等輕車都尉世職，諡壯敏。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and a hereditary second-rank commandant of light chariots, with the posthumous title Zhuangmin (Stalwart and Alert).
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent with a second-rank light-chariot commandancy, posthumous name Zhuangmin (Stalwart and Alert).

sentences.zh: 恩長，赫舍里氏，滿洲鑲紅旗人。

translations.literal: En Chang, of the Heseri clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: En Chang of the Heseri clan was a Bordered Red Banner Manchu.

sentences.zh: 由親軍、十五善射，累遷安徽寧國營副將。

translations.literal: From imperial bodyguard and master of the Fifteen Perfect Shots he was promoted repeatedly to deputy commander of the Ningguo battalion in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: From imperial bodyguard and master archer he rose to deputy commander of Anhui's Ningguo battalion.

sentences.zh: 道光中治江防，被獎。

translations.literal: In the Daoguang period he managed Yangtze defenses and was rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: Under Daoguang he worked on Yangtze defenses and won commendation.

sentences.zh: 累擢壽春鎮總兵。

translations.literal: He was promoted repeatedly to commander of the Shouchun garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in stages to commander of the Shouchun garrison.

sentences.zh: 初率兵守安慶，陸建瀛赴九江上游，調充翼長，為軍鋒。

translations.literal: At first he led troops to hold Anqing; when Lu Jianying went to the upper reaches at Jiujiang he was transferred to serve as wing commander and vanguard of the army.
translations.idiomatic: He first held Anqing; when Lu Jianying went upstream to Jiujiang he was made wing commander and army vanguard.

sentences.zh: 與賊戰江中，毀賊船三十餘艘，眾寡不敵，死之。

translations.literal: He fought the rebels on the river, destroyed more than thirty rebel boats, but was outnumbered and died.
translations.idiomatic: He fought the rebels on the river, destroyed more than thirty of their boats, but was overwhelmed and killed.

sentences.zh: 贈提督，予騎都尉兼雲騎尉世職，諡武壯。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted provincial military commissioner and a hereditary commandant of cavalry combined with commandant of the cloud cavalry, with the posthumous title Wuzhuang (Martial and Stalwart).
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously made provincial military commissioner with a combined cavalry and cloud-cavalry commandancy, posthumous name Wuzhuang (Martial and Stalwart).

sentences.zh: 陳勝元，福建同安人。

translations.literal: Chen Shengyuan was a native of Tong'an in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shengyuan came from Tong'an, Fujian.

sentences.zh: 由行伍歷官福建參將。

translations.literal: From the ranks he rose through offices to Fujian brigade commander.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from the ranks to brigade commander in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 捕洋盜有功，累擢江南福山鎮總兵。

translations.literal: He had merit in capturing foreign pirates and was promoted repeatedly to commander of the Fushan garrison in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: For capturing foreign pirates he was promoted to commander of Jiangnan's Fushan garrison.

sentences.zh: 率水師防江，賊至太平四合山，迎擊，追至蕪湖，中砲落水，死之。

translations.literal: He led the naval force to defend the river; when the rebels reached Sihe Mountain in Taiping he met the attack, pursued them to Wuhu, was struck by cannon fire, fell into the water, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Leading the fleet on river defense, he met the rebels at Sihe Mountain in Taiping, pursued them to Wuhu, was hit by cannon fire, fell into the water, and drowned.

sentences.zh: 贈提督，予騎都尉世職，諡剛勇。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted provincial military commissioner and a hereditary commandant of cavalry, with the posthumous title Gangyong (Bold and Brave).
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously made provincial military commissioner with a hereditary cavalry commandancy, posthumous name Gangyong (Bold and Brave).

sentences.zh: 祁宿藻，字幼章，山西壽陽人，大學士俊藻弟也。

translations.literal: Qi Suzao, style Youzhang, was a native of Shouyang in Shanxi and younger brother of Grand Secretary Junzao.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Suzao, courtesy name Youzhang, was from Shouyang, Shanxi, and younger brother of Grand Secretary Qi Junzao.

sentences.zh: 道光十八年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Daoguang he passed the metropolitan examination, was selected a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed an editor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1838 he passed the metropolitan examination, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and became an editor.

sentences.zh: 以召對受宣宗知，特簡授湖北黃州知府，調武昌。

translations.literal: Because of an audience he won the Daoguang Emperor's notice and was specially appointed prefect of Huangzhou in Hubei, then transferred to Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial audience won him the Daoguang Emperor's favor; he was appointed prefect of Huangzhou in Hubei, then moved to Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 連年大水，城幾沒，堵禦獲全。

translations.literal: For successive years great floods nearly submerged the city, but by blocking and defending it was preserved intact.
translations.idiomatic: Year after year great floods nearly drowned the city, but he held the dikes and kept it intact.

sentences.zh: 治急賑，煮粥施錢及衣棺藥餌，全活災民甚眾，政聲最。

translations.literal: He managed emergency relief, distributing congee, money, clothing, coffins, and medicines, and saved a great many disaster victims; his reputation for governance was foremost.
translations.idiomatic: He ran emergency relief—gruel, cash, clothes, coffins, and medicine—and saved countless victims; his reputation for governance was unmatched.

sentences.zh: 超擢廣東鹽運使，遷按察使，又遷湖南布政使。

translations.literal: He was promoted out of turn to Guangdong salt transport commissioner, then transferred to provincial surveillance commissioner, and again to Hunan provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was jumped to Guangdong salt commissioner, then surveillance commissioner, then Hunan administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 會韶州數縣土匪起，詔留宿藻督兵往剿，七戰皆捷，匪首就擒。

translations.literal: When bandits rose in several counties of Shaozhou, an edict kept Suzao to lead troops to suppress them; in seven battles he was victorious each time and the bandit chieftain was captured.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits rose in several Shaozhou counties, he was kept to lead troops against them, won seven battles in a row, and took the chief.

sentences.zh: 事平，賜花翎。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled he was granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: When order was restored he received the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 調江寧布政使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Jiangning provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Jiangning administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，河決豐北，山東、江北皆被水。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng the Yellow River broke at Fengbei and Shandong and Jiangbei were inundated.
translations.idiomatic: In 1851 the Yellow River burst at Fengbei and flooded Shandong and the north bank region.

sentences.zh: 大學士杜受田奉命臨賑，疏請以宿藻督辦江北賑務，章程出其手定，奏頒兩省行之。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Du Shoutian was ordered to oversee relief on the spot and memorialized that Suzao should supervise Jiangbei relief affairs; the regulations were drawn up by his own hand, memorialized, and promulgated for implementation in the two provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Du Shoutian was sent to oversee relief and asked that Suzao run Jiangbei relief; the regulations were drafted by Suzao, approved, and applied in both provinces.

sentences.zh: 及粵匪將東下，宿藻馳返江寧，括庫儲治軍械，盡移兵糈及南門外商市囤米入城，號召義勇之士備戰守。

translations.literal: When the Cantonese rebels were about to move east, Suzao raced back to Jiangning, drew on the treasury to prepare arms, moved all military grain and the rice hoarded by foreign merchants at the South Gate market into the city, and called up volunteers to prepare for war and defense.
translations.idiomatic: As the rebels marched east he rushed back to Nanjing, spent the treasury on arms, moved all military grain and foreign merchants' rice at the South Gate into the city, and rallied volunteers for defense.

sentences.zh: 見督撫倉皇失措，各存意見，勸諫不聽，乃偕祥厚等密疏上聞。

translations.literal: Seeing the governor and governor-general flustered and each holding his own view, he urged them but was not heeded; he then joined Xianghou and others in a secret memorial to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Finding the governor and governor-general panicked and at odds, he pleaded with them in vain, then joined Xianghou and others in a secret memorial.

sentences.zh: 建瀛既被罪失眾心，宿藻獨任事，賊至，力疾登陴指揮，曆三晝夜，城大兵單，援師不至，知事不可為，在城上嘔血數升，卒。

translations.literal: After Jianying was punished and lost the people's hearts, Suzao alone shouldered the work; when the rebels arrived he forced himself, though ill, onto the battlements to command; for three days and nights he held on; the city was large and the army few; relief did not come; knowing the affair could not be saved, he vomited several sheng of blood on the wall and died.
translations.idiomatic: After Jianying's disgrace Suzao alone bore the burden; when the rebels came he dragged himself to the wall though ill and directed the fight for three days and nights; the city was vast, the troops few, and no relief came; seeing all was lost, he vomited blood on the ramparts and died.

sentences.zh: 文宗悼惜，加等優血卩，贈右都御史，廕一子以知州用。

translations.literal: The Wenzong Emperor mourned him, granted enhanced posthumous honors, posthumously made him Right Censor-in-Chief, and ennobled one son for appointment as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong mourned him, granted enhanced honors, posthumously made him Right Censor-in-Chief, and ennobled one son for prefectural appointment.

sentences.zh: 同治初，江南平，兄俊藻遣尋其遺櫬，得之城北僻地。

translations.literal: In the early Tongzhi period, when Jiangnan was pacified, his elder brother Junzao sent men to seek his coffin and found it in a secluded place north of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tongzhi, after Jiangnan was pacified, his brother Junzao sent men to find his coffin in a lonely spot north of the city.

sentences.zh: 曾國籓以聞，請附祀祥厚專祠，追諡文節。

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan reported this and requested that he be attached for worship at Xianghou's special shrine, with the posthumous title Wenjie (Cultivated and Principled) conferred in retrospect.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan reported it and asked that he be worshipped at Xianghou's shrine, with the posthumous name Wenjie (Cultivated and Principled).

sentences.zh: 當城陷時，署布政使鹽巡道塗文鈞、江安糧道陳克讓、江寧知府魏亨逵、同知承恩、通判程文榮、上元知縣劉同纓、江寧知縣張行澍同死之。

translations.literal: When the city fell, acting provincial administration commissioner and salt circuit intendant Tu Wenjun, Jiang'an grain commissioner Chen Kerang, Jiangning prefect Wei Hengkui, subprefect Cheng'en, assistant prefect Cheng Wenrong, Shangyuan county magistrate Liu Tongying, and Jiangning county magistrate Zhang Xingshu all died together.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, acting administration commissioner and salt intendant Tu Wenjun, Jiang'an grain commissioner Chen Kerang, Nanjing prefect Wei Hengkui, subprefect Cheng'en, assistant prefect Cheng Wenrong, Shangyuan magistrate Liu Tongying, and Jiangning magistrate Zhang Xingshu all died.

sentences.zh: 克讓，奉天承德人。

translations.literal: Kerang was a native of Chengde in Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Kerang was from Chengde in Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 道光三年進士，授吏部主事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daoguang he passed the metropolitan examination and was appointed a principal clerk in the Board of Civil Office.
translations.idiomatic: In 1823 he passed the metropolitan examination and was made a principal clerk in the Board of Civil Appointments.

sentences.zh: 累擢四川綏遠知府，調成都。

translations.literal: He was promoted repeatedly to prefect of Suiyuan in Sichuan and was transferred to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to prefect of Suiyuan in Sichuan, then was transferred to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，擢江安糧道，居官清正。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng he was promoted to Jiang'an grain commissioner and was upright in office.
translations.idiomatic: In 1851 he became Jiang'an grain commissioner and was known for integrity.

sentences.zh: 賊將至，或勸以督運出。

translations.literal: When the rebels were about to arrive, some urged him to supervise grain transport and leave.
translations.idiomatic: As the rebels approached, some urged him to supervise grain shipments and leave the city.

sentences.zh: 克讓曰：「江寧東南都會，失則大局危。

translations.literal: Kerang said: 'Jiangning is the great metropolis of the southeast; if it is lost the larger situation is endangered.
translations.idiomatic: Kerang said, 'Nanjing is the great metropolis of the southeast; if it falls the whole situation is endangered.

sentences.zh: 去將焉往？

translations.literal: If I go, where shall I go?
translations.idiomatic: Where would I go?

sentences.zh: 」又請徙其孥，其妻泣曰：「去為民望，不如死！

translations.literal: ' Others again asked him to move his family; his wife wept and said: 'To leave would be to abandon the people's hope; better to die!
translations.idiomatic: ' When others asked him to move his family, his wife wept and said, 'To flee would abandon the people's hope; better to die!

sentences.zh: 」宿藻死而不瞑，克讓撫之曰：「庫尚有儲金，當​​募死士以成君志。

translations.literal: ' When Suzao died his eyes would not close; Kerang comforted him and said: 'There is still stored silver in the treasury; we must recruit men willing to die to fulfill your purpose.
translations.idiomatic: ' Suzao died with open eyes; Kerang comforted him, saying, 'There is still silver in the treasury; we must hire men willing to die to finish your work.

sentences.zh: 」克讓守清涼山，督兵戰，殞於陣。

translations.literal: ' Kerang held Qingliang Hill, directed the troops in battle, and fell on the field.
translations.idiomatic: ' Kerang held Qingliang Hill, led the fight, and was killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 弟克誠，子鬆恩，同遇害。

translations.literal: His younger brother Ke Cheng and son Song'en were murdered together with him.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Ke Cheng and son Song'en were killed with him.

sentences.zh: 妻李，自經死。

translations.literal: His wife Li hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Li hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 賜卹，予騎都尉世職，本籍請建專祠，追諡忠節。

translations.literal: Grants of condolence were bestowed and a hereditary commandant of cavalry was given; his native place requested a special shrine, and the posthumous title Zhongjie (Loyal and Principled) was conferred in retrospect.
translations.idiomatic: Condolence grants and a hereditary cavalry commandancy were awarded; his home district asked for a private shrine and the posthumous name Zhongjie (Loyal and Principled).

sentences.zh: 同纓，江西石城人。

translations.literal: Tongying was a native of Shicheng in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tongying was from Shicheng, Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 拔貢。

translations.literal: He was a tribute student from the provincial school.
translations.idiomatic: He entered official life as a tribute student.

sentences.zh: 歷官鹽城、泰興、江浦、上元、六合、江寧諸縣，皆有聲。

translations.literal: He served in succession as magistrate of Yancheng, Taixing, Jiangpu, Shangyuan, Liuhe, and Jiangning, and everywhere won reputation.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate at Yancheng, Taixing, Jiangpu, Shangyuan, Liuhe, and Jiangning, winning a name at each post.

sentences.zh: 江寧治防，儲糧練團，胥賴其力。

translations.literal: In preparing Jiangning's defenses, storing grain and drilling militia, all relied on his strength.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing's defenses, grain stores, and militia drill all depended on him.

sentences.zh: 賊初至，假向榮書請入城，同纓察其詐，卻之。

translations.literal: When the rebels first arrived they forged a letter from Xiang Rong requesting entry to the city; Tongying detected the fraud and refused them.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels first came they forged a letter from Xiang Rong asking entry; Tongying saw the fraud and refused.

sentences.zh: 砲裂城，率死士禦擊复完。

translations.literal: When cannon fire split the wall he led dare-to-die troops to beat back the attack and restore the breach.
translations.idiomatic: When cannon fire breached the wall he led picked men to beat back the assault and repair the gap.

sentences.zh: 及城陷，賦絕命詞，投水死，卹典加等，贈道銜，諡武烈。

translations.literal: When the city fell he composed a death poem and drowned himself; condolence honors were raised a grade, he was posthumously granted circuit intendant rank, and honored with the posthumous title Wulie (Martial and Ardent).
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he wrote a final poem and drowned himself; honors were raised a grade, he was posthumously given circuit rank, and named Wulie (Martial and Ardent).

sentences.zh: 瑞昌，字云閣，鈕祜祿氏，滿洲鑲黃旗人。

translations.literal: Rui Chang, style Yunge, of the Niohuru clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Rui Chang, courtesy name Yunge, of the Niohuru clan, was a Bordered Yellow Banner Manchu.

sentences.zh: 六世祖敖德，以軍功予騎都尉世職。

translations.literal: His sixth-generation ancestor Aode received a hereditary commandant of cavalry for military merit.
translations.idiomatic: His sixth-generation ancestor Aode received a hereditary cavalry commandancy for military merit.

sentences.zh: 瑞昌由拜唐阿授鑾儀衛整儀尉，累遷冠軍使。

translations.literal: Rui Chang entered service through the Tangya post and was appointed Ceremonial Guard orderly officer of the Imperial Procession Guard, and was promoted repeatedly to champion commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Rui Chang entered through the Tangya post, became an Imperial Procession Guard orderly, and rose to champion commissioner.

sentences.zh: 道光二十九年，擢正白旗漢軍副都統，歷金州、吉林副都統。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year of Daoguang he was promoted to deputy lieutenant-general of the Plain White Banner Han Army and served in succession as deputy lieutenant-general at Jinzhou and Jilin.
translations.idiomatic: In 1849 he became Plain White Banner Han Army deputy lieutenant-general and served at Jinzhou and Jilin.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，擢杭州將軍，未之任，率盛京兵赴淮、徐，專辦山東防剿。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng he was promoted to military governor of Hangzhou; before he took up the post he led Shengjing troops to Huai and Xu to specialize in Shandong defense and suppression.
translations.idiomatic: In 1853 he was appointed Hangzhou military governor; before taking office he led Shengjing troops to the Huai–Xu region to handle Shandong defense.

sentences.zh: 尋從僧格林沁、勝保勦賊畿輔。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he followed Sengge Rinchen and Sheng Bao in suppressing rebels in the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined Sengge Rinchen and Sheng Bao in suppressing rebels around the capital.

sentences.zh: 四年，連戰靜海、河間、東光。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he fought repeatedly at Jinghai, Hejian, and Dongguang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1854 he fought at Jinghai, Hejian, and Dongguang.

sentences.zh: 五年，會攻連鎮，扼河西，毀賊巢木城。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he joined the assault on Lianzhen, held the west bank of the river, and destroyed the rebels' wooden stockade.
translations.idiomatic: In 1855 he helped assault Lianzhen, held the west bank, and destroyed the rebels' wooden fort.

sentences.zh: 賊首林鳳祥就擒，被詔嘉獎，命赴本任。

translations.literal: The rebel leader Lin Fengxiang was captured; he received an edict of commendation and was ordered to proceed to his regular post.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel leader Lin Fengxiang was captured; the throne commended him and ordered him to his post.

sentences.zh: 十年二月，粵匪由廣德入浙境，省城兵單，分防湖州、孝豐、餘杭。

translations.literal: In the second month of the tenth year the Cantonese rebels entered Zhejiang from Guangde; the provincial capital had few troops and detachments were posted to Huzhou, Xiaofeng, and Yuhang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of 1860 the rebels entered Zhejiang from Guangde; the capital was weakly garrisoned and troops were split to Huzhou, Xiaofeng, and Yuhang.

sentences.zh: 賊分股突犯杭州，瑞昌令副都統來存出武林門御之，自守錢塘門，偕巡撫羅遵殿佈置甫定，賊已麕至，縱火撲城。

translations.literal: Rebel detachments suddenly struck Hangzhou; Rui Chang ordered deputy lieutenant-general Lai Cun to go out through Wulin Gate to meet them while he himself held Qiantang Gate; he had just finished arrangements with Governor Luo Zundian when the rebels swarmed up, set fires, and pressed the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel columns struck Hangzhou; Rui Chang sent Deputy Lieutenant-General Lai Cun out Wulin Gate while he held Qiantang Gate; he and Governor Luo Zundian had barely finished arrangements when the rebels swarmed in, set fires, and assaulted the walls.

sentences.zh: 越十日，地雷發，城陷。

translations.literal: After more than ten days a land mine exploded and the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: After ten days a mine blew open the wall and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 瑞昌率旗兵迎擊於湧金門，殺傷相當。

translations.literal: Rui Chang led the banner troops to meet the attack at Yongjin Gate; casualties were about equal on both sides.
translations.idiomatic: Rui Chang led banner troops to meet them at Yongjin Gate with heavy losses on both sides.

sentences.zh: 退守駐防子城，賊屢攻，力拒卻之。

translations.literal: He fell back to hold the garrison sub-city; the rebels attacked repeatedly but were driven back by force.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew to the garrison sub-city; the rebels attacked again and again but were beaten back.

sentences.zh: 相持六日，會張玉良率援兵至，夾擊，賊棄城走，遂復杭州，特詔嘉獎，賜黃馬褂，予二等輕車都尉世職。

translations.literal: The standoff lasted six days; then Zhang Yuliang arrived with relief troops; attacking from both sides they drove the rebels to abandon the city and flee, and Hangzhou was recovered; a special edict commended him, granted the yellow riding jacket, and gave a hereditary second-rank commandant of light chariots.
translations.idiomatic: After six days Zhang Yuliang came with relief; attacking from both sides they drove the rebels out and recovered Hangzhou; the throne specially commended him, gave a yellow riding jacket, and a hereditary second-rank light-chariot commandancy.

sentences.zh: 既而江南大營潰，常、蘇兩郡陷。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the great Jiangnan camp collapsed and Changzhou and Suzhou both fell.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the great Jiangnan camp collapsed and Changzhou and Suzhou were lost.

sentences.zh: 張玉良以罪黜，命瑞昌總統江南諸軍，江長貴副之，規復甦州，而賊已陷長興、武康，复諭先顧杭城，再圖進取。

translations.literal: Zhang Yuliang was dismissed for crime; Rui Chang was ordered to take overall command of the Jiangnan armies with Jiang Changgui as his deputy, planning to recover Suzhou, but the rebels had already taken Changxing and Wukang; he was again instructed to secure Hangzhou first and then plan advance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yuliang was dismissed; Rui Chang was made overall commander of Jiangnan forces with Jiang Changgui as deputy to recover Suzhou, but the rebels had taken Changxing and Wukang; he was told to hold Hangzhou first.

sentences.zh: 嘉興尋為賊踞，命瑞昌督張玉良往攻，亦未果。

translations.literal: Jiaxing was soon occupied by rebels; Rui Chang was ordered to supervise Zhang Yuliang in attacking it, but that too failed.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaxing soon fell; Rui Chang was ordered to direct Zhang Yuliang's attack, which also failed.

sentences.zh: 十月，賊陷富陽、餘杭，复撲杭州，瑞昌親督副都統傑純、副將吳再升擊走之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the rebels took Fuyang and Yuhang and again struck Hangzhou; Rui Chang personally directed deputy lieutenant-general Jie Chun and brigade commander Wu Zaisheng to beat them back.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the rebels took Fuyang and Yuhang and struck Hangzhou again; Rui Chang personally led Jie Chun and Wu Zaisheng to drive them off.

sentences.zh: 十一年，賊勢益張，由嘉興進陷石門，湖州亦被圍，浙東諸郡相繼失守。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year rebel strength grew greater; advancing from Jiaxing they took Shimen; Huzhou was also besieged; the prefectures of eastern Zhejiang fell in succession.
translations.idiomatic: In 1861 rebel power grew; they advanced from Jiaxing, took Shimen, besieged Huzhou, and eastern Zhejiang's prefectures fell one after another.

sentences.zh: 自紹興為賊踞，杭州愈危，遂被圍，瑞昌偕巡撫王有齡嬰城固守逾兩月。

translations.literal: Once Shaoxing was held by rebels Hangzhou grew more perilous and was besieged; Rui Chang together with Governor Wang Youling held the city in a desperate defense for more than two months.
translations.idiomatic: After Shaoxing fell Hangzhou grew desperate and was besieged; Rui Chang and Governor Wang Youling held the walls for over two months.

sentences.zh: 張玉良戰城下，傷殞，軍心益渙。

translations.literal: Zhang Yuliang fought below the walls, was wounded and died; army morale grew still more scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yuliang fought below the walls, was wounded and killed, and morale collapsed further.

sentences.zh: 外援不至，糧道皆絕。

translations.literal: Outside relief did not come and all grain routes were cut.
translations.idiomatic: No relief came and all supply lines were cut.

sentences.zh: 瑞昌憂憤成疾，旗兵精壯多傷亡，乃集將校，誓死報國，家給火藥。

translations.literal: Rui Chang, worried and indignant, fell ill; many of the sturdy banner soldiers had been killed or wounded; he then gathered his officers, swore to die for the state, and distributed gunpowder to every household.
translations.idiomatic: Rui Chang fell ill with grief and anger; many bannermen were dead or wounded; he gathered his officers, swore to die for the state, and gave each household gunpowder.

sentences.zh: 及城陷，瑞昌先舉火自焚，闔營次第火起，同死者，杭州副都統關福及江蘇糧儲道赫特赫納以下男婦四千餘人。

translations.literal: When the city fell Rui Chang first set fire and burned himself; fires rose in succession through the whole camp; those who died with him included Hangzhou deputy lieutenant-general Guan Fu and Jiangsu grain commissioner Hetehena and more than four thousand men and women below them in rank.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell Rui Chang set himself on fire first; fires spread through the camp; Hangzhou Deputy Lieutenant-General Guan Fu, Jiangsu grain commissioner Hetehena, and more than four thousand men and women died with him.

sentences.zh: 事聞，詔優恤，贈太子太保，晉一等輕車都尉世職，諡忠壯。

translations.literal: When the affair was reported, an edict granted enhanced condolence; he was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, his hereditary rank was raised one grade to first-rank commandant of light chariots, and he was given the posthumous title Zhongzhuang (Loyal and Stalwart).
translations.idiomatic: On report the throne granted enhanced honors, posthumously made him Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, raised his hereditary rank one grade, and named him Zhongzhuang (Loyal and Stalwart).

sentences.zh: 入祀京師昭忠祠，杭州建專祠，死事者附祀焉。

translations.literal: He was entered in the capital Shrine of Loyalty and Martyrdom; a special shrine was built at Hangzhou, and those who died in the affair were attached for joint worship.
translations.idiomatic: He was enshrined in the capital Shrine of Loyalty and Martyrdom, given a private shrine at Hangzhou, with other victims worshipped beside him.

sentences.zh: 同治三年，杭州复，左宗棠奏瑞昌妾吳，於城破時挈兩幼子緒成、緒恩出走失散。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tongzhi, after Hangzhou was recovered, Zuo Zongtang memorialized that Rui Chang's concubine Wu, when the city fell, took the two young sons Xucheng and Xu'en and fled but was separated from them.
translations.idiomatic: In 1864, after Hangzhou was recovered, Zuo Zongtang reported that Rui Chang's concubine Wu fled the fallen city with sons Xucheng and Xu'en but was separated from them.

sentences.zh: 事定，尋得緒恩，護送回京。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled Xu'en was soon found and escorted back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: After order was restored Xu'en was found and escorted to the capital.

sentences.zh: 詔念瑞昌忠烈，命本旗傳交其長子內閣中書緒光收養，飭宗棠購訪緒成下落，迄未得。

translations.literal: An edict, mindful of Rui Chang's loyal martyrdom, ordered his banner to hand over his eldest son, Hanlin bachelor Xuguang, for adoption, and directed Zongtang to purchase and search for Xucheng's whereabouts, but he was never found.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of Rui Chang's martyrdom, the throne ordered his banner to place his eldest son Xuguang, a Hanlin bachelor, in adoption, and told Zuo Zongtang to search for Xucheng, who was never found.

sentences.zh: 後以兩世職並為三等子爵。

translations.literal: Later the two hereditary offices were combined into a third-rank marquisate.
translations.idiomatic: Later his two hereditary offices were merged into a third-rank marquisate.

sentences.zh: 傑純，布庫魯氏，蒙古正白旗人，杭州駐防。

translations.literal: Jie Chun, of the Bokuru clan, was a Mongol of the Plain White Banner, garrisoned at Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jie Chun of the Bokuru clan was a Plain White Banner Mongol of the Hangzhou garrison.

sentences.zh: 由驍騎校累遷協領。

translations.literal: From valiant cavalry captain he was promoted repeatedly to assistant commandant.
translations.idiomatic: From valiant cavalry captain he rose to assistant commandant.

sentences.zh: 忠勇得士心，為瑞昌所倚。

translations.literal: Loyal and brave, he won the soldiers' hearts and was relied on by Rui Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Brave and loyal, he won the troops' hearts and was Rui Chang's right hand.

sentences.zh: 杭州初破，瑞昌欲自剄，傑純與副都統來存言賊以偏師疾至，未有後繼，猶可力保駐防城以待外援，瑞昌從之，乃登陴守禦。

translations.literal: When Hangzhou first fell Rui Chang wished to cut his own throat; Jie Chun together with deputy lieutenant-general Lai Cun said the rebels had come with only a detached force in haste and had no follow-up troops, and the garrison city could still be held by force to await outside relief; Rui Chang followed this advice and went up on the battlements to defend.
translations.idiomatic: When Hangzhou first fell Rui Chang meant to kill himself; Jie Chun and Lai Cun said the rebels were only a fast detachment with no reserves, and the garrison city could still be held for relief; Rui Chang agreed and took the wall.

sentences.zh: 傑純當武林門，日與賊戰，長子前鋒校納蘇鏗陣亡，不之顧，殮其屍，不哭，曰：「汝先得所歸矣！

translations.literal: Jie Chun held Wulin Gate and fought the rebels daily; his eldest son, vanguard company officer Nasukeng, died in battle; he paid no heed, buried the body, and did not weep, saying: 'You have found your resting place first!
translations.idiomatic: Jie Chun held Wulin Gate and fought daily; his eldest son Nasukeng, a vanguard officer, was killed; he buried him without weeping and said, 'You have found your home first!

sentences.zh: 」及援兵至，怒馬突出，賊披靡，追擊出城十里外。

translations.literal: ' When relief troops arrived he charged out on a furious horse; the rebels scattered; he pursued them more than ten li beyond the city.
translations.idiomatic: ' When relief came he charged out on a furious horse, scattered the rebels, and pursued them ten li beyond the walls.

sentences.zh: 以復城功，賜花翎。

translations.literal: For the merit of recovering the city he was granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: For recovering the city he received the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 擢寧夏副都統，留浙協同團練大臣統率練勇，出省复富陽。

translations.literal: He was promoted to deputy lieutenant-general of Ningxia but remained in Zhejiang to assist the militia training commissioner in commanding trained militia and went out of the province to recover Fuyang.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Ningxia deputy lieutenant-general, he stayed in Zhejiang to help the militia commissioner and led trained militia to recover Fuyang.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，賊复犯杭州，迎剿於觀音橋，手刃數賊，率西湖水勇截擊，斬馘甚眾，又連破撲城之賊，追至留下，進克餘杭，賜號額騰伊巴圖魯。

translations.literal: That winter the rebels again attacked Hangzhou; he met them in suppression at Guanyin Bridge, cut down several rebels with his own hand, led West Lake water braves in interception, beheaded and counted ears in great number, broke successive assaults on the walls, pursued to Liuxia, advanced and recovered Yuhang, and was granted the title Erteng I Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, when rebels struck Hangzhou again, he met them at Guanyin Bridge, killed several with his own hand, led West Lake water fighters in ambush, killed many, broke repeated assaults, pursued to Liuxia, retook Yuhang, and received the title Erteng I Batulu.

sentences.zh: 調授乍浦副都統，仍留防省城。

translations.literal: He was transferred to deputy lieutenant-general of Zhapu but still remained to defend the provincial capital.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Zhapu deputy lieutenant-general, he still stayed to defend the capital.

sentences.zh: 十一年，城再陷，傑純戰一晝夜，所部傷亡略盡，遣次子出避，以存宗祀，闔門自焚，獨策馬入賊陣，死之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the city fell a second time; Jie Chun fought one day and one night; his command was nearly all killed or wounded; he sent his second son away to escape in order to preserve the clan line; the whole household burned themselves; he alone spurred his horse into the rebel ranks and died.
translations.idiomatic: In 1861 the city fell again; Jie Chun fought a day and a night until his force was nearly gone; he sent his second son away to save the line, burned his household, and alone charged the rebel ranks to his death.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉其一門忠烈，依都統例賜卹，予騎都尉兼雲騎尉世職，杭州、乍浦並建專祠，子婦孫僕皆附祀。

translations.literal: An edict praised the loyal martyrdom of his whole household, granted condolence according to the lieutenant-general precedent, gave a hereditary commandant of cavalry combined with commandant of the cloud cavalry, and built special shrines at both Hangzhou and Zhapu; sons, daughters-in-law, grandchildren, and servants were all attached for worship.
translations.idiomatic: The throne praised his household's martyrdom, granted lieutenant-general honors, a combined cavalry and cloud-cavalry commandancy, and shrines at Hangzhou and Zhapu with sons, daughters-in-law, grandchildren, and servants worshipped there.

sentences.zh: 後復加恩入祀京師昭忠祠，諡果毅。

translations.literal: Later additional favor was shown by entry in the capital Shrine of Loyalty and Martyrdom, with the posthumous title Guoyi (Resolute).
translations.idiomatic: Later he was further honored in the capital Shrine of Loyalty and Martyrdom with the posthumous name Guoyi (Resolute).

sentences.zh: 擢次子固魯鏗知府，改歸京旗。

translations.literal: His second son Gurukeng was promoted to prefect and transferred to the capital banner.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Gurukeng was made prefect and transferred to a capital banner.

sentences.zh: 錫齡阿，扎哈蘇氏，蒙古正白旗人，荊州駐防。

translations.literal: Xi Ling'a, of the Zahasu clan, was a Mongol of the Plain White Banner, garrisoned at Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Ling'a of the Zahasu clan was a Plain White Banner Mongol of the Jingzhou garrison.

sentences.zh: 以佐領率兵從戰沔陽、監利、潛江、應城、漢陽、宜昌。

translations.literal: As assistant commandant he led troops in campaigns at Mianyang, Jianli, Qianjiang, Yingcheng, Hanyang, and Yichang.
translations.idiomatic: As assistant commandant he fought at Mianyang, Jianli, Qianjiang, Yingcheng, Hanyang, and Yichang.

sentences.zh: 積功累擢福州副都統，調乍浦副都統。

translations.literal: By accumulated merit he was promoted repeatedly to deputy lieutenant-general of Fuzhou and transferred to deputy lieutenant-general of Zhapu.
translations.idiomatic: By merit he rose to Fuzhou deputy lieutenant-general, then Zhapu deputy lieutenant-general.

sentences.zh: 十一年，賊來犯，督兵出戰，城中內應起，折回巷戰，全軍皆沒，與兩子榮輝、榮耀同殞於陣。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year when rebels came to attack he directed troops out to fight; an inside response rose in the city; he turned back to fight in the lanes; the whole army was destroyed; he and his two sons Ronghui and Rongyao all fell on the field together.
translations.idiomatic: In 1861, when rebels attacked, he led troops out; collaborators rose inside the city; he fought back in the lanes; his whole force was destroyed; he and sons Ronghui and Rongyao died together.

sentences.zh: 贈都統銜，予騎都尉兼雲騎尉世職，諡武烈，入祀京師昭忠祠。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted lieutenant-general rank, given a hereditary commandant of cavalry combined with commandant of the cloud cavalry, with the posthumous title Wulie (Martial and Ardent), and entered in the capital Shrine of Loyalty and Martyrdom.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously made lieutenant-general with a combined cavalry and cloud-cavalry commandancy, posthumous name Wulie (Martial and Ardent), enshrined in the capital Shrine of Loyalty and Martyrdom.

sentences.zh: 嗣以荊州紳民感念保境功，請建專祠。

translations.literal: Later the gentry and people of Jingzhou, mindful of his merit in protecting the territory, requested a special shrine.
translations.idiomatic: Later Jingzhou's gentry, grateful for his defense of the region, asked for a private shrine.

sentences.zh: 子榮輝、榮耀並予雲騎尉世職。

translations.literal: His sons Ronghui and Rongyao were both given hereditary commandant of the cloud cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Sons Ronghui and Rongyao both received hereditary cloud-cavalry commandancies.

sentences.zh: 論曰：清製，行省要區置旗兵駐防，其尤重都會，兵額多者，以將軍領之。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Under Qing institutions, in important provincial areas banner troops were stationed on garrison duty; where the post was especially weighty, as at great capitals with larger quotas, a military governor led them.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: Under Qing rule, banner garrisons were posted in key provinces; at the greatest capitals, with the largest quotas, a military governor commanded them.

sentences.zh: 蓋監製疆臣，備不虞也。

translations.literal: This was to oversee and restrain the provincial governor and prepare against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: The intent was to watch the civil governor and guard against surprise.

sentences.zh: 承平恬嬉，非復國初勁旅，小有變動，可資鎮懾；

translations.literal: In long peace they grew complacent and were no longer the fierce troops of the dynasty's founding; for small disturbances they could still serve to awe and suppress;
translations.idiomatic: In long peace they grew soft and were no longer the founding dynasty's fierce troops; small troubles they could still overawe;

sentences.zh: 鉅寇燎原，力不足以御之。

translations.literal: when a great rebel blaze spread across the land their strength was not enough to withstand it.
translations.idiomatic: but when a great rebellion blazed across the empire they lacked the strength to resist.

sentences.zh: 江南之失，誤於陸建瀛不預設防。

translations.literal: The loss of Jiangnan was due to Lu Jianying's failure to set defenses in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangnan was lost because Lu Jianying failed to prepare defenses.

sentences.zh: 祥厚倉猝專任，以孤城當方張之寇，寧有幸焉。

translations.literal: Xianghou, suddenly placed in sole charge, with a lone city faced a rebel force in full expansion—how could he have had good fortune?
translations.idiomatic: Xianghou, thrust suddenly into sole command, held a lone city against a rising power—what chance had he?

sentences.zh: 杭州初陷，賊僅偏師，故瑞昌能守內城以待援；

translations.literal: When Hangzhou first fell the rebels were only a detached column, so Rui Chang could hold the inner city and wait for relief;
translations.idiomatic: When Hangzhou first fell the rebels were only a detachment, so Rui Chang could hold the inner city for relief;

sentences.zh: 及蘇、常既失，輔車無依，終不能保，大勢然也。

translations.literal: once Suzhou and Changzhou were lost and the supporting states had nothing to lean on, in the end it could not be preserved—the larger trend was so.
translations.idiomatic: once Suzhou and Changzhou were lost and the flank was gone, the city could not be saved—the tide of events demanded it.

sentences.zh: 然二人者，皆能以忠義激勵，城亡與亡，婦嬰皆知效死，烈已！

translations.literal: Yet both men were able to rouse others through loyalty and righteousness; when the city perished they perished with it; even women and infants knew how to die in service—how ardent!
translations.idiomatic: Yet both roused others by loyalty and righteousness, perished with their cities, and even women and children chose death—how fierce their devotion!

sentences.zh: 祁宿藻孤忠盡瘁，傑純智勇能軍，並一時傑出之才。

translations.literal: Qi Suzao exhausted himself in solitary loyalty; Jie Chun was wise, brave, and able in command of armies; all were outstanding talents of their time.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Suzao gave his all in loyal service; Jie Chun combined wisdom, courage, and command of troops—outstanding men of their day.

sentences.zh: 炎岡同燼，世尤惜之。

translations.literal: Flames on the same ridge burned together; the age especially mourns them.
translations.idiomatic: They perished like flames on the same ridge, and the age mourns them all the more.
